_notes.title: The page's name, shown top left. Movie Night when left out.
_notes.people: Everyone who hearts films on this device, one to eight names. The turn chip passes between them.
_notes.films: The watch list, in the order the wall shows it. Each film has a title and a year, and can have a note (one line under the title), a poster (a .jpg, .jpeg, .png, or .webp path in your project), and hearts (names from people). A film with no poster key still finds posters/<title-year>.jpg in your project, for example posters/knives-out-2019.jpg.
_notes.theme: cinema (red velvet and a warm spotlight), drive-in (a night sky and neon), or arthouse (gallery paper and a cool lamp). Each has a light and a dark room, following the device's setting.
_notes.watched: Films already seen, with the date (2026-10-17) and stars from 0 to 5. They start the Watched shelf; the page adds to it from then on.
_notes.lookupPosters: true lets the page look up a missing poster on Wikipedia when it is online; false keeps every request on your own server.
_notes.TMDB_READ_TOKEN: Optional, set with csc key set. When it is set, run.py fetches a poster from TMDB for each film with no poster file and saves it into the page.
